correctness.rationale: For an ideal (S,T), the minimal excluded elements are precisely the vertices outside S and the edges of E(S) outside T. Over a triple fixed by rho cubed each vertex is absent at most once. On each edge, t_(i+1)=a_i-t_i, where a_i indicates that both endpoints belong to S_i. Thus 2t_0=a_0+a_2-a_1, excluding odd weight of (a_0,a_1,a_2). This excludes edges within the always-present vertex set X and edges between distinct missing-time classes. For an edge of class j (both endpoints in X union Y_j, not both in X), the unique edge state is at j+2 modulo three. Consequently every always-present vertex must be supplied by newly selected edges from each class in turn, exactly the three-neighbour-colour condition. Conversely S_i=V minus Y_i and T_i=E(G[X union Y_(i+1)]) give E(S_i)=T_i disjoint union T_(i+1); the endpoints of T_(i+1) are exactly X union Y_(i+2), by the neighbour condition and absence of isolated vertices. This recovers both parts of rowmotion. No ideal is fixed (a proper ideal acquires a minimal omitted element, and the full ideal goes to the empty ideal). The cyclic action on colourings is free since V minus X is nonempty. In a biclique a nonempty admissible X must be a whole shore (otherwise G-X is connected), leaving the surjection count 3^t-3*2^t+3 on the other shore; for maximum degree at most two no nonempty X is admissible. A fresh minimal-complement versus component-colouring enumeration compared orbit sets and all three reconstructed transitions on all 43 connected labelled graphs of orders two through four; this is corroboration only. The frozen 771-graph and other reported tests were not replayed.
residual_risks: The independent test is bounded to graphs of orders two through four; the theorem for larger graphs follows from the proof, not from the test. No formal verification is claimed.

evidence: The first two inspected passages establish general actions, not a criterion for their period-three states on graph incidence posets. Rowmotion on fences concerns a path-shaped poset family, not arbitrary incidence graphs.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Knowing the action exists or is a product of toggles does not solve its fixed-by-third-iterate constraint; the edge parity and converse construction are substantive extra steps.

evidence: At a=1 and a=2 the frozen biclique expression reduces to the same 3^(b-1)-2^b+2. A whole-shore count does not show that arbitrary missing-time classes are unions of components or that every admissible colouring yields an orbit.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The special-family conclusions do not imply the asserted general bijection. The proof must both extract the three-colour neighbour constraint and recover the ideals; neither direction follows by a parameter substitution into those counts.

value.rationale: The bijection classifies the actual orbits, replaces iteration over order ideals by a static test on independent cuts and coloured components, and isolates the precise structural obstruction for a non-universal three-cycle. It is useful beyond verifying isolated period counts; no efficiency guarantee for evaluating the sum is assumed.
residual_risks: Value is confined to period three in the stated graph class; there is no analogous assertion for all orbit lengths.
